currentContext.business: Abril Paper Tech Limited manufactures sublimation heat transfer paper in 30, 65, 75 and 90 GSM specifications, each grade designed for a different need in the sublimation printing process, from light and delicate transfers to more robust and detailed printing tasks. The Company operates two coating lines, sources quality-grade half-white shade virgin base paper directly from paper manufacturers and their dealers, and applies specialized coating chemicals with an emphasis on consistent coating quality and preservation of the base paper. It markets through its own in-house sales team to digital textile printers across garments, hosiery, apparel and home furnishings, and reports a single business segment: manufacturing and trading of paper and paper products.

Manufacturing and Trading of Paper and P: Coated sublimation paper rolls in widths of 24 to 72 inches

currentContext.expansion: The Company's expansion narrative for FY26 is framed around its September 2025 SME listing rather than a named, dated project. It completed an IPO of a fresh issue of 22,00,000 equity shares at an issue price of Rs 61 per equity share aggregating Rs 13.42 Crores, listed on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on September 5, 2025, and states that the proceeds are being utilised for the objects stated in the Prospectus, which strengthened the capital base and left the balance sheet deleveraged and re-capitalized. Operationally the Company runs two coating lines at its single manufacturing facility at Jolva, Palsana, Surat, Gujarat. Management's stated expansion intent is capital expenditure towards 'state-of-the-art coating expansions' that would take the Company from a localized regional supplier to a high-capacity national player, alongside using the newly infused working capital to broaden its footprint into non-Gujarat markets, deeper into southern and northern textile clusters such as Tirupur and Ludhiana, and to explore South Asian and Middle Eastern export corridors. No project name, rupee quantum, capacity addition or commissioning timeline is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
currentContext.mdna: Digital Textile Boom: demand for high-quality sublimation paper is heavily driven by advancements in digital textile printing across garments, hosiery, apparel and home furnishings|Shift to Sustainable Media: industrial textile printers are increasingly moving away from traditional dyeing towards digital heat transfer techniques to optimize water consumption and reduce environmental footprints, which management says positions the company's product lineup within contemporary demand curves|Indian paper and paper products market grew from USD 8.6 billion in 2018 to USD 13.4 billion by 2024, a CAGR of 7.8%, with India accounting for roughly 5% of world paper production and among the top 15 paper-producing countries|Government-backed initiatives, including the Central Pulp and Research Institute's work on testing facilities for specialty paper and paper boards and HRD frameworks, are said to foster an environment ripe for high-value specialty paper investments|Post-IPO the balance sheet has been deleveraged and re-capitalized, which management frames as the enabler for expansion|Management describes the strategic horizon as 'exceptionally positive'

risks.note: The Company operates out of one manufacturing facility at Surat (Jolva, Palsana), Gujarat, which management says exposes operations to geographical concentration risk from local and regional factors that may adversely affect its business, results of operations and cash flows. Management notes that apart from COVID-19 related operational restrictions it has not experienced any material disruption at the facility in the past.

risks.risk: Dependence on third-party utilities (electricity, water and fuel)
risks.note: The business depends on an adequate and uninterrupted supply of electricity, water and fuel procured from third parties for the manufacturing facility; a shortage or breakdown in supply is outside the Company's control to correct.

risks.risk: Raw-material price volatility and supply shortage
risks.note: The Company depends significantly on key raw materials -- base paper and coating compounds -- to produce sublimation heat transfer paper rolls, exposing it to price volatility and supply shortages. Base paper is sourced from paper manufacturers and their dealers rather than produced in-house.

Management explicitly states an objective to 'mitigate customer concentration' by broadening its footprint into non-Gujarat markets, which identifies existing concentration in its customer base as a live structural exposure.

The Company reports only one business segment -- manufacturing and trading of paper and paper products -- and operates in the niche domain of sublimation heat transfer paper (30-90 GSM) for digital printing, so demand, pricing and technology shifts in digital textile printing bear on the entire business with no offsetting segment.

risks.risk: Small scale and thin operating team relative to a newly listed public company
risks.note: As on 31st March 2026 there were 16 permanent employees on the payroll, and the transition from a closely held partnership firm to a listed public limited entity has 'mandated a systematic professionalization of the human resource framework', indicating governance and process build-out is still in progress.

risks.risk: Execution risk on deployment of IPO proceeds
risks.note: The September 2025 fresh issue raised Rs 13.42 Crore whose proceeds 'are being utilized for the objects stated in the Prospectus'; the stated coating expansion and non-Gujarat market entry carry no disclosed project name, quantum or commissioning timeline, so returns on the newly infused capital remain unproven.
